incident-bot: PAGING: p99 latency SLO breach on production continuous-batching path. p95 crossed 350ms, p99 ~1.2s, increased error rate for streaming sessions. auto-created incident ID INC-2026-031.

alex: ack, oncall here. seeing spikes across us-west-2 clusters. starting a quick triage. who is oncall infra? @maya?

maya: i'm here. looking at metrics now. p95 jumped from 110ms -> ~420ms at 10:12 UTC. p99 peaked 1.22s. streaming stalls flagged where token generation stalls for 200-400ms between tokens.

jia: logs show batch size distribution shifted up; tail of batch sizes more heavy. suspect mixed sequence lengths causing long queues while scheduler waits to fill large batch.

sam: repeating: are we seeing preemption happening? i see multiple preempt events 10:11-10:14 UTC on gpu-node-17.

maya: yes preemption traces show long KV-copy/evict ops. KV eviction rate spiked ~3x, causing GC-like stalls. agents show top-keys eviction per-request increased.

alex: immediate mitigations to try:
- reduce max_batch_bytes / max_batch_tokens on the cont-batching path
- enable aggressive small-seqlen binning (route small seqs to fast lane)
- fallback heavy sequences to non-continuous streaming or dedicated pool

jia: i'm going to flip batch_max_size 32 -> 16 on the canary pool (usw2-canary-1). will also set batch_fill_timeout 8ms -> 4ms. command:

```
# set canary config
rbctl set-config --pool usw2-canary-1 --batch_max_size=16 --batch_fill_timeout_ms=4
```

maya: i'll route 5% heavy-seq traffic to dedicated-proxy to relieve cont-batch lanes. doing canary routing change now.

ops-bot: Deploy started: routing-rule update id=rr-884 at 10:18 UTC. Rolling in 20s.

sam: after config changes p95 dropped to ~180ms on canary, p99 down to ~420ms. streaming stalls reduced on canary.

alex: good. let's promote to 25% for all us-west clusters and keep monitoring for 10m.

maya: promoted. watching SLOs.

(2m later)

maya: improvement but some nodes still showing tail >800ms. digging into scheduling fairness: scheduler logs show large sequences held priority and prevented smaller seqs from being batched, leading to starvation. fair-share algorithm may not account for seq-length skew.

jia: putting up a short-term rule: cap batch aggregate tokens per-batch to 4096 so large sequences don't monopolize. command:

```
rbctl set-config --pool global --max_batch_tokens=4096
```

sam: rolling that; also evicting stale KV shards on node-17 to reduce eviction overhead.

ops-bot: Job kv-evict node-17 started. ETA 45s.

alex: customer impact: two customers reported increased latency on high token requests; no data loss; sessions resumed after routing changes. marking severity as P2.

maya: adding note: watch embeddings/embedding-job interference — background jobs started around 09:50 UTC and may have contributed to resource contention.

jia: long-term actions noted in ticket: improve seq-length aware scheduler, introduce fast-lane for short sequences, enhance KV eviction to be async, add configurable token-cap per-batch, and automated heavy-seq routing to dedicated pools.

alex: created INC-2026-031 with mitigations and timeline. handing off to night oncall @sam for monitoring and follow-up. please escalate if p99 > 1s again.

sam: ack, taking oncall. leaving the current routing and batch caps in place. will follow up with a postmortem draft.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-031 acknowledged by sam. Pager cleared for alex/maya/jia.

alex: thanks team. leaving some notes in the ticket about metrics to collect: per-batch token histogram, per-node KV-eviction latency, preemption counts, and streaming token-gap distributions.

maya: will attach logs and the canary eval graphs to INC-2026-031.

jia: I'll open a PR for scheduler change and add unit tests for seq-length fairness.

sam: handover complete. monitoring alert thresholds adjusted: p95 alert -> 250ms, p99 alert -> 800ms for next 12h.

(react: :thumbsup: )
